meta.title: Tenoko Ski Resort
meta.description: Right off Route 113—Showa retro Kamoshika Lodge, a rare schlepplift, uncrowded local snow play, and an Iide onsen loop.

hero.title:
Tenoko
Ski Resort
hero.tagline: Retro cafeteria charm and a rare schlepplift—enjoy uncrowded local snow at a private-feel ski park.

transit.title:
Right off Route 113,
walkable from Tenoko Station.
transit.lead: Past Michi-no-Eki Iide on Route 113—flat access makes it easier to reach by car without steep snowy roads. From Tenoko Station (JR Uetsu Main Line), it is about 15–20 minutes on foot (~1.2 km). After flood damage, replacement buses may run—check service before you go.
specs: 15–20 min walk from Tenoko Station (~1.2 km)
transit.imgAlt: Winter drive on Route 113 toward Tenoko Ski Resort in Iide, Yamagata

primary.title: Showa retro × private-feel snow
primary.lead: At the center house Kamoshika Lodge, ramen and curry are around ¥700. With fewer visitors, the slopes stay fresh—enjoy quality wet snow and powder in a near-private atmosphere.
primary.imgAlt: Retro cafeteria charm at Kamoshika Lodge and quiet Tenoko snow

secondary.title: Rare schlepplift with mid-station drop
secondary.lead: No chairlifts—only a 445 m schlepplift and rope tow. The nationally rare mid-station drop lets less-fit beginners start partway down.

pass.title:
After skiing,
Yonezawa beef & onsen.
pass.lead: Bundle concept: Tenoko lift ticket + Kaminoyu Hotel or Shirasagi Onsen entry + Michi-no-Eki Iide product coupons. Turn single-site spend into an area tour.
pass.noticeBody: No single-ride tickets are available. To use lifts, you generally need at least a coupon book (adult ¥1,100). This is a short-term proposal to reduce opportunity loss for light visitors.
pass.imgAlt: Skiing paired with Iide onsen and local Yonezawa beef—an easy day-trip model

rental.title:
Arrive empty-handed,
play in the snow.
rental.lead: For Route 113 drive visitors—rent a car near Shinjo Station and reach the hill via flat winter roads. Promote sled and tube snow play that does not require ski skills.
rental.whisper: QR payments (PayPay, etc.) are proposed to remove cash friction (report ch.6).
rental.imgAlt: Families starting snow play with rental gear—hands-free visit image

yukinko.title:
Tue Thu Fri Sat
night skiing.
yukinko.lead: Lit night skiing on Tue Thu Fri Sat—locals after work and Route 113 road visitors can practice basics comfortably.
yukinko.whisper: Kamoshika Lodge offers ramen/curry around ¥700 after your runs.
yukinko.imgAlt: Night-lit slopes at Tenoko Ski Resort—quiet local winter evening

family.title:
Local warmth,
room to play.
family.lead: A gentle family slope and a wide central run—practice without crowd pressure. Tube sliding, popular during the 2022 lift outage, is recommended as a permanent attraction.
specs: Parking right in front of the slopes
family.noticeBody: Surface lifts are tough for snowboard beginners—snow-play stays (ski, sled, tubes) fit best.
family.imgAlt: Families snow-playing near Kamoshika Lodge—uncrowded local resort feel

workation.title:
Morning snow,
lunch at the lodge, evening bath.
workation.lead: Morning snow at Tenoko → lunch at Kamoshika Lodge or nearby diners → soak at Kaminoyu or Shirasagi → Michi-no-Eki Iide for souvenirs. A day-trip winter loop model.

local.title: Showa retro × near-private local guide
local.body: 700-yen ramen at Kamoshika Lodge, 44+ year schlepplift, and fresh uncrowded snow—share with #ShowaRetro and #EmoSki.

schools.title: Iide winter full-set ticket
schools.body: Mutual discounts linking onsen, Michi-no-Eki coupons, and lift tickets—aim for higher area spending per person.

summer.title: Real Japan winter trip for curious travelers
summer.body: A Showa-era local hill with virtually no foreign visitors—pair ¥700 ramen with an English-friendly menu and Michi-no-Eki tie-ins as a deep local JAPOW experience.
